title: Bonus Episode: Your Boss is Watching You. Is that OK? with Dave Tomczak

sentences.en: Hi everyone, it's Kaitlyn Luna, host of Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是《心理学说话》的主持人凯特琳·卢娜。

sentences.en: This episode was recorded during
sentences.zh: 本期节目是在

sentences.en: APA's Technology, Mind, and Society conference held in October 2019 in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 美国心理学协会于2019年10月在华盛顿特区举办的“技术、心灵与社会”会议期间录制的。

sentences.en: I was on maternity leave during that time, so my colleague Kim Mills was a guest hoSt.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在休产假，所以我的同事金·米尔斯担任了客座主持人。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoy this episode.
sentences.zh: 希望大家喜欢这期节目。

sentences.en: Hello, and welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a bi-weekly podcast from the American Psychological Association that explores the breadth and depth of psychological science.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是一档由美国心理学协会制作的双周播客，带您探索心理学科学的广度与深度。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Do you ever get the feeling at work that you're being watched?
sentences.zh: 你在工作中是否有时会觉得有人在盯着你？

sentences.en: To a certain degree you are, and it's possible that you will soon be tracked even more closely by your employer, whether that's through video surveillance, GPS location tracking,
sentences.zh: 某种程度上确实如此，而且你可能很快就会受到雇主更密切的追踪，无论是通过视频监控、GPS定位追踪、

sentences.en: or internet monitoring.
sentences.zh: 还是互联网监控。

sentences.en: If that disturbs you, you're not alone.
sentences.zh: 如果这让你感到不安，你并不孤单。

sentences.en: Our guest today has been doing research into how much workplace surveillance is acceptable to employees, and at what point do people feel that the nosy boss has gone too far?
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾一直在研究员工能接受多少程度的工作场所监控，以及在什么节点人们会觉得好管闲事的上司管得太宽了？

sentences.en: David Tomchek is a product solutions consultant at Aon, a global professional services firm.
sentences.zh: 大卫·汤姆切克是怡安集团的一名产品解决方案顾问，怡安是一家全球专业服务公司。

sentences.en: He is also working toward his PhD in industrial organizational psychology at the George Washington University, where he has researched the influence
sentences.zh: 他目前还在乔治华盛顿大学攻读工业与组织心理学博士学位，在那里他研究了

sentences.en: of electronic performance monitoring on employee behaviors.
sentences.zh: 电子绩效监控对员工行为的影响。

sentences.en: His interests also include personal environment fit, occupational health psychology, and corporate social responsibility.
sentences.zh: 他的兴趣还包括个人与环境契合度、职业健康心理学以及企业社会责任。

sentences.en: Welcome, David Tomchek.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，大卫·汤姆切克。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Glad to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: So why do our bosses want to track what we're doing all day?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么我们的老板想要追踪我们一整天都在做什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, Americans have a reputation for high productivity, which presumably means that we work pretty hard.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美国人以高生产率闻名，这大概意味着我们工作相当努力。

sentences.en: Is that not right?
sentences.zh: 难道不是吗？

sentences.en: I would definitely agree that we do work hard.
sentences.zh: 我绝对同意我们工作很努力。

sentences.en: I think in terms of what we have going on in the current sphere of big data, we have a lot of technologies out there that are capable of gathering
sentences.zh: 我认为就我们目前所处的大数据时代而言，我们有很多技术能够

sentences.en: large amounts of employee behavioral data in relatively short periods of time and relatively easily.
sentences.zh: 在相对较短的时间内、相对轻松地收集大量的员工行为数据。

sentences.en: To add on to that, we have artificial intelligence, algorithms, and machine learning that can kind
sentences.zh: 除此之外，我们还有人工智能、算法和机器学习，它们可以

sentences.en: of wrangle these big sets of data and perhaps give us some meaningful implications about employee behavior.
sentences.zh: 处理这些庞大的数据集，或许能为我们提供一些关于员工行为的有意义的启示。

sentences.en: Whether or not that actually is indicative of employee performance is sometimes subject to criticism.
sentences.zh: 这是否真正能指示员工绩效，有时会受到批评。

sentences.en: But I think what employers want to do right now is to make the best use of all of that
sentences.zh: 但我认为雇主现在想做的是充分利用他们拥有的所有

sentences.en: data they have and use that to inform productivity and performance or even guide safety or health behaviors.
sentences.zh: 数据，并以此来指导生产力和绩效，甚至指导安全或健康行为。

sentences.en: So what are employers interested in learning through these tactics?
sentences.zh: 那么雇主有兴趣通过这些策略了解什么呢？

sentences.en: Are their motivations beneficent for the most part or do we even know?
sentences.zh: 他们的动机在很大程度上是善意的吗？或者我们甚至无从得知？

sentences.en: That's the big question.
sentences.zh: 这才是最大的问题。

sentences.en: So what we find is that a lot of organizations don't actually tell employees that they're being monitored.
sentences.zh: 我们发现很多组织实际上并没有告诉员工他们正在被监控。

sentences.en: And they don't tell them exactly, and if they are being monitored, they don't tell them when, how, or in what context they are being monitored.
sentences.zh: 他们没有明确告知，即使在被监控，他们也没有告诉员工何时、如何以及在什么背景下被监控。

sentences.en: I think what a lot of organizations are hoping is that there are some sort of small
sentences.zh: 我想很多组织希望的是，有一些

sentences.en: employee behaviors that can sort of give some sort of credence to other aspects of job performance that we've traditionally tried to capture just by performance appraisal.
sentences.zh: 微小的员工行为能够为传统上我们仅通过绩效评估试图捕捉的工作绩效的其他方面提供某种信度。

sentences.en: So for example, we have some organizations that are looking at facial expressions, voice intonation in meetings,
sentences.zh: 所以例如，有些组织在会议中观察面部表情、语调，

sentences.en: seeing how frequently people talk up or talk over other individuals.
sentences.zh: 看看人们发言的频率或者打断别人说话的频率。

sentences.en: And a lot of that can be good.
sentences.zh: 其中很多是好事。

sentences.en: We can tell somebody after a meeting and say, hey, judging from our sociometric badge that we had on you, it seems like you're talking over individuals quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在会后对某个人说，嘿，从我们发给你的社交测定胸牌来看，你似乎经常打断别人说话。

sentences.en: You're not giving your followers enough opportunity to chime in with any sort of creative problem solving that they have.
sentences.zh: 你没有给你的下属足够的空间来提出他们自己的任何创造性问题解决方案。

sentences.en: So in that circumstance,
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情况下，

sentences.en: we can get very minute aspects of job performance saying these are the specific situations in which
sentences.zh: 我们可以了解工作绩效的极其微小的方面，说明这些是具体的场景，

sentences.en: perhaps you could work on something instead of maybe saving all of that for the end of the year performance appraisal where some of those small behaviors might go overlooked.
sentences.zh: 在这些场景中，也许你可以改进某些方面，而不必把所有这些都留到年终绩效评估时去说，那时其中一些细微的行为可能已经被忽视了。

sentences.en: So a lot of what we're looking at is, is there meaning from very small aspects of behavior and how can that inform job performance?
sentences.zh: 所以我们研究的很大一部分是，极微小的行为方面是否有意义，以及这如何能够指导工作绩效？

sentences.en: That's got me going down two, two trails here.
sentences.zh: 这让我的思绪走向了两个不同的方向。

sentences.en: One is, first of all, you mentioned biometric badges, but can you explain that?
sentences.zh: 首先，你提到了生物识别胸牌，你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: And I mean, are they happening already?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些事情已经在发生了吗？

sentences.en: Are people wearing these things?
sentences.zh: 人们在佩戴这些东西吗？

sentences.en: So, so they call these sociometric badges.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们把这些称为社交测定胸牌。

sentences.en: Sorry, sociometric.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，是社交测定。

sentences.en: So this is something that was started, I believe, in 2015 by MIT.
sentences.zh: 所以这是麻省理工学院在2015年左右开始的一项研究。

sentences.en: They were looking at sociometric badges and looking to see how often we could get such rich forms of data intra-individual.
sentences.zh: 他们当时在研究社交测定胸牌，看看我们能以多高的频率获取个体内部如此丰富的数据形式。

sentences.en: So lots of performance or behavioral data within the individual.
sentences.zh: 也就是个人内部大量的绩效或行为数据。

sentences.en: And what they, what they're supposed to do is that, so an individual wears this badge perhaps around their neck with a lanyard.
sentences.zh: 它们的作用是，个人可以把这个胸牌挂在脖子上，用挂绳挂着。

sentences.en: And this badge is just continually taking in any sort of audio information that they have within a meeting.
sentences.zh: 这个胸牌会持续不断地接收他们在会议中的任何音频信息。

sentences.en: I don't think that this is used widely right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为目前这还没有被广泛使用。

sentences.en: But if you think about where certain technologies are going nowadays, where a lot
sentences.zh: 但如果你想想某些技术如今的发展方向，其中许多技术

sentences.en: of them have these sorts of capabilities, when we think about all the things that your smartphone can do, the modern iPhone has facial recognition.
sentences.zh: 都具备这些功能，当我们想到智能手机能做所有事情时，现代iPhone就有人脸识别功能。

sentences.en: It has a very good microphone.
sentences.zh: 它有一个非常好的麦克风。

sentences.en: It tracks all of your internet behaviors.
sentences.zh: 它追踪你所有的互联网行为。

sentences.en: What we have right now are technologies that are going to be capable of kind of taking in a lot of this information.
sentences.zh: 我们现在拥有的技术将有能力接收大量这类信息。

sentences.en: And I don't think it's used very often now, but certainly there is some research indicating that it is trending towards that direction.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它现在经常被使用，但当然有一些研究表明它正朝着那个方向发展。

sentences.en: So the other path my mind was going down when you started talking about this was, I mean, you know, I've worked in many offices and there are people who talk over other people.
sentences.zh: 当我开始谈论这个时，我脑海中浮现的另一条思路是，我的意思是，你知道，我在许多办公室工作过，总有人喜欢打断别人说话。

sentences.en: I mean, we all kind of know that, you know, Joe over there is a jerk in meetings.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们都知道，你知道，那边的乔在会议上是个讨厌鬼。

sentences.en: So is this just giving the employer some kind of coverage to be able to say, I have data that proves that you're a jerk in meetings?
sentences.zh: 所以这只是给雇主提供某种掩护，让他们能够说：“我有数据证明你在会议上是个讨厌鬼”？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I think a lot of people have a resistance to criticism, especially anything that's negative.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得很多人对批评都有抵触情绪，尤其是任何负面的东西。

sentences.en: And when you can actually show them the data and say, hey, 60% of the time that you're talking, you're talking over somebody, or you have just repeated
sentences.zh: 而当你真正向他们展示数据并说，嘿，在你说话的时间里，有60%你在打断别人，或者你只是重复了

sentences.en: their idea and sort of steamrolled that individual, people might be more willing to accept that when
sentences.zh: 他们的观点并且有点压制了那个人，当有实际证据支持他们可能行为不当的事实时，人们可能更愿意接受这一点。

sentences.en: there's actual evidence to support the fact that perhaps they're behaving incorrectly.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，这些技术目前还没有被广泛使用，但它们正在萌芽阶段。

sentences.en: But again, these are technologies that are not used extensively at this point, but they are kind of burgeoning.
sentences.zh: 所以现在使用它的那些地方，我们仅仅是在谈论科技公司吗？

sentences.en: So the kinds of places that are using it now, are we just talking about tech companies?
sentences.zh: 这就像是硅谷的事情吗？

sentences.en: Is this like a Silicon Valley thing?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以它只会在非常亲技术的公司里有非常、非常小的使用范围。

sentences.en: So it would be very, very small usage in very tech-friendly companies.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 所以你的研究探讨了员工心中的界限。

sentences.en: So your research looked at the limits in the minds of employees.
sentences.zh: 你发现什么样的监视（如果你愿意这么称呼的话）算是过度了？

sentences.en: And what did you find how much spying, if you will, is too much?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在研究中想要探讨的是本质上，对监控的期望是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: So what we wanted to look at with our research was essentially, where do expectations of monitoring come from?
sentences.zh: 有很多研究表明监控是对隐私的侵犯。

sentences.en: We have a lot of research saying that monitoring is an invasion of privacy.
sentences.zh: 这对员工来说被认为是不公平的，但我们很好奇这如何根据个人、他们从事的工作或组织的环境而有所不同。

sentences.en: It's considered not fair to employees, but we're kind of curious about how that differs based on the individual or the job that they're in or the context of the organization.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们的研究借鉴了心理契约文献，该文献基本指出，个人对雇主有着这些未明言的期望。

sentences.en: So we looked at our research from the psychological contract literature, which basically states that individuals have these unstated expectations of their employer.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上期望雇主尊重他们，并期望雇主足够信任他们能够完成工作。

sentences.en: They basically expect their employer to treat them with respect, and they expect that their employer trusts them enough to do the job.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想要看看的是，好吧，如果你在所有可能的方式下都被监控，假设EPM（电子绩效监控）的数量增加。

sentences.en: And so what we wanted to see is, okay, if you're being monitored in every possible way, let's say the amount of EPM increases.
sentences.zh: 你是——所以EPM是——EPM就是电子绩效监控。

sentences.en: You are- So EPM is- EPM is electronic performance monitoring.
sentences.zh: 所以也许你的电脑活动受到监控，你的电子邮件被阅读，还有音视频监控。

sentences.en: So perhaps you're being, you have your computer activity monitored, your emails being read, there's audio video surveillance.
sentences.zh: 随着EPM数量的增加，我们基本上想说，好吧，这将是对心理契约的违背。

sentences.en: As that amount of EPM increases, we wanted to basically say, okay, it's going to be a violation of the psychological contract.
sentences.zh: 这可能会导致个人的行为实际上与EPM试图实现的目标相矛盾。

sentences.en: And this might lead individuals to behave in a way that is actually contradictory to what EPM tries to do.
sentences.zh: EPM试图做的是引导人们做出某些行为。

sentences.en: What EPM tries to do is direct people towards certain behaviors.
sentences.zh: 当我们监控某事时，我们基本上是在向员工发出信号，表明这很重要。

sentences.en: When we monitor something, we are basically giving a signal to the employee saying that this matters.
sentences.zh: 然而我们发现，随着监控水平的提高，一个人经历这种情况为心理

sentences.en: What we find, though, is that as the level of monitoring increases, the likelihood that a person experiences that as a psychological
sentences.zh: 契约违背的可能性也会增加，并实际上导致他们对组织有所保留地付出努力。

sentences.en: contract violation increases and actually leads them to withhold effort from the organization.
sentences.zh: 所以我们得到的结果与EPM试图实现的完全相反。

sentences.en: So we're getting the exact opposite of what EPM is trying to do.
sentences.zh: 有些人看到这种违背可能会说，好吧，那我休息时间要延长一点。

sentences.en: We have people who might look at this violation and say, okay, well, I'm going to take longer on my breaks.
sentences.zh: 我可能会迟到。

sentences.en: I might show up late.
sentences.zh: 他们以非常隐蔽而非公开的方式这样做。

sentences.en: And they do this in very covert ways rather than overt.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是因为当然了，他们正在被监控。

sentences.en: They do ways that, because of course, they are being monitored.
sentences.zh: 他们的行为受到监控，他们没有能力，你知道，去偷窃组织的东西或诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Their actions are being monitored and they don't have the ability to, you know, steal from the organization or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 所以也许他们会从组织那里偷走时间。

sentences.en: So perhaps they steal time from the organization.
sentences.zh: 那么工作类型或行业之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: So what are the differences among job types or industries?
sentences.zh: 你也在研究这个吗？

sentences.en: You're looking at that as well?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 所以我们从两个不同的角度来研究这个问题。

sentences.en: So we looked at that from two different angles.
sentences.zh: 我们首先从工作态度角度来看，也就是工作自主性。

sentences.en: We looked at first from the job attitudes angle, which would be job autonomy.
sentences.zh: 这是个人对其在安排工作、如何处理某个任务等方面所拥有的自主权的感知。

sentences.en: This is the perception that an individual has over the discretion that they have over maybe scheduling their work, how they go about a certain task and so forth.
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现，嗯，当EPM与个人对工作自主性的感知相匹配时，我们的，嗯，心理契约违背感是最小的。

sentences.en: So what we found was that, um, when EPM and the person's perception of job autonomy match, that's when we have the least amount of, uh, psychological contract violation.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上这就是说，对工作自主性有高度感知、坚信自己

sentences.en: So basically what that's saying is that individuals who have high perceptions of job autonomy, the belief that they
sentences.zh: 可以随心所欲地完成工作的人，当这种状态与低EPM相结合时，

sentences.en: can do, um, their work as they wish when that, when that is coupled with, um, low EPM.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这些员工没有受到高度监控。

sentences.en: So, uh, these individuals are not being monitored heavily.
sentences.zh: 他们最不可能报告任何形式的心理契约违背。

sentences.en: They are the least likely to report any sort of psychological contract violation.
sentences.zh: 现在，这种效应在增加监控数量并限制该人完成工作能力时会强烈增加。

sentences.en: Now that, uh, effect strongly increases when you increase the number of monitoring and limit that person's ability to do, to do their job.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，嗯，当人们对自主性的感知较低时，嗯，EPM似乎没有任何影响。

sentences.en: And interestingly enough, uh, when people have low perceptions of autonomy, uh, EPM does not appear to have any sort of effect.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些人同样倾向于，嗯，感知到违背，就像，你知道，高自主性的人处于高EPM，嗯，情况下一样。

sentences.en: Um, those people are just as likely to, um, perceive violation as, you know, a high autonomy individual in a high EPM, uh, situation.
sentences.zh: 那么就哪些可以监控、哪些不可以监控而言，员工目前在工作场所有什么权利？

sentences.en: So what rights do employees have in the workplace right now in terms of what can and can't be monitored?
sentences.zh: 是否存在法律限制，还是这完全是一个勇敢的新世界？

sentences.en: Are there legal limits or is this all just sort of a brave new world?
sentences.zh: 现在是一个有趣的时期，因为欧盟出台了通用数据保护条例。

sentences.en: It's an interesting time right now because of the, uh, general data protection regulations from, uh, the EU.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们仅从美国来看，嗯，员工并没有很多权利。

sentences.en: So if we look at it just from the U S, um, employees do not have a lot of rights.
sentences.zh: 隐私法自1984年以来就没有更新过，除了我认为

sentences.en: Uh, the privacy laws have not been updated since 1984 with the exception of, I think
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州最近对其法律进行了一些隐私更新。

sentences.en: California has recently had some sort of privacy updates to their laws.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，1984年，在人们现在被监控的方式方面，这并没有给我们

sentences.en: But again, 1984, that doesn't really give us, um, a lot of leeway in terms of what's going on with how people are being monitored now.
sentences.zh: 提供太多的余地。

sentences.en: The thing is, is that a lot of, uh, organizations are becoming global or, uh, international.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，许多，嗯，组织正在变得全球化或，嗯，国际化。

sentences.en: And so they actually have to adopt, uh, GDPR, um, rules.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们实际上不得不采纳，嗯，GDPR的规则。

sentences.en: So what we'll be seeing soon is that, uh, organizations will be taking this a lot more seriously or, uh, at least address monitoring upfront.
sentences.zh: 所以我们很快就会看到，嗯，组织会更严肃对待这一点，或者，嗯，至少会公开解决监控问题。

sentences.en: But right now employees in the United States, considering if it's just, uh, an American company do not have many rights.
sentences.zh: 但目前美国的员工，如果考虑到这只是一家美国公司，并没有多少权利。

sentences.en: Um, there's actually no law that says that they need to be informed when they are being monitored, which is, um, a huge problem, especially from the literature side.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上没有任何法律规定他们在被监控时必须被告知，这，嗯，是一个巨大的问题，特别是在文献方面。

sentences.en: And is that happening in the companies that are doing it right now?
sentences.zh: 现在正在这样做的公司里情况是这样的吗？

sentences.en: Are they revealing to employees?
sentences.zh: 他们向员工透露了吗？

sentences.en: Let's say when you, you know, go to human resources, you've accepted the job and they give you all the paperwork that you have to fill out.
sentences.zh: 比方说当你，你知道，去人力资源部门，你已经接受了工作，他们给你所有需要填写的纸质文件。

sentences.en: Is there a form that says, oh, and by the way, you know, we're going to be monitoring you.
sentences.zh: 是否有一张表格写着，哦，顺便说一句，你知道，我们要监控你。

sentences.en: We're not only watching whether you're shopping on Amazon all day, but we also want to know what your skin conductance is and we're tracking your eye movements
sentences.zh: 我们不仅在看你是否整天在亚马逊上购物，我们还想知道你的皮肤电导率，我们在追踪你的眼球运动

sentences.en: or, you know, whatever they might be looking at.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，无论他们可能在看什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I believe there's a statistic out there that says about 20% of organizations actually fully inform their employees about when, where, and how they're being monitored.
sentences.zh: 我相信有一个统计数据表明，大约20%的组织真正全面告知了员工他们何时、何地以及如何被监控。

sentences.en: So this does not really happen very often.
sentences.zh: 所以这种情况其实并不常见。

sentences.en: Um, I can say from my experience, uh, working for various organizations, I've never had that conversation, but I think, uh,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我可以从我为各种组织工作的经验说，我从来没有过那种对话，但我认为，嗯，

sentences.en: right now we can just kind of assume, uh, a lot of, uh, everything is being monitored.
sentences.zh: 现在我们只能假设，嗯，很多，嗯，一切都在被监控。

sentences.en: Uh, we have records of everything, every single mouse click, any, any sort of action that you do on your computer is recorded and can be accessed at any time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们有一切的记录，每一次鼠标点击，你在电脑上做的任何、任何动作都被记录下来，并且可以随时访问。

sentences.en: So I think some people will, uh, regardless just sort of operate under, I am being monitored.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为有些人会，嗯，无论如何只是在“我正在被监控”的假设下运作。

sentences.en: I just expect it.
sentences.zh: 我只是对此有预期。

sentences.en: And our research actually supports that, that a lot of individuals say that I just expect to be monitored nowadays.
sentences.zh: 我们的研究实际上也支持这一点，许多人表示我如今只是预期会被监控。

sentences.en: I don't have to be told.
sentences.zh: 我不需要被告知。

sentences.en: I know that things are being recorded and can be accessed later.
sentences.zh: 我知道事情正在被记录并且以后可以被访问。

sentences.en: Are there differences, uh, among age cohorts?
sentences.zh: 不同年龄段的人之间有什么差异吗，嗯？

sentences.en: I'm thinking just millennials.
sentences.zh: 我只是在想千禧一代。

sentences.en: I mean, people who are digital natives who kind of grew up in this world, that they seem to be less protective of their personal privacy than say baby boomers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这样一个世界中长大的数字原住民，他们似乎比婴儿潮一代等人群对个人隐私的保护意识要低。

sentences.en: Are you finding that in terms of being watched on the job?
sentences.zh: 你在工作中被监视这方面发现这种情况了吗？

sentences.en: We haven't actually explored age effects, but there has been some research out there that
sentences.zh: 我们实际上还没有探讨过年龄效应，但有一些研究

sentences.en: has kind of showed, uh, uh, in, in a comical way, how much, um, young people are willing to give up some of their personal information for very small things.
sentences.zh: 以一种带有喜剧色彩的方式展示了年轻人为了微不足道的小东西愿意放弃多少个人信息。

sentences.en: Uh, for one example, uh, they found that college students were very willing to give up personal information for a free slice of pizza.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们发现大学生为了免费的一片披萨，非常愿意交出个人信息。

sentences.en: And so, uh, I think there will be some differences.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这其中会存在一些差异。

sentences.en: I think there's a generation, uh, of people growing up that have constantly had access to a phone that records their conversations.
sentences.zh: 我认为有一代人成长起来了，他们随时都能接触到会记录他们对话的手机。

sentences.en: Um, and I think they're getting very used to it, but I don't have any research to support that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想他们已经对此习以为常了，不过我没有相关的研究来支持这一说法。

sentences.en: Maybe something we'll look at to in the future.
sentences.zh: 也许这是我们以后会关注的课题。

sentences.en: So are, are people looking at the right things at this point?
sentences.zh: 那么，目前人们关注的方向对吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm, I'm thinking, I believe where I work, they've implemented something that sort of looks at your calendar and maybe your key strokes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，据我所知，在我工作的地方，他们实施了一种系统，可以查看你的日程表，也许还有你的键盘敲击情况。

sentences.en: I'm not sure what they're looking at.
sentences.zh: 我不确定他们具体在看什么。

sentences.en: And they kind of tell you whether you, you had a day where you were sort of relaxed compared to other days, but does that matter?
sentences.zh: 他们会告诉你，与往常相比，你今天是不是相对轻松，但这有意义吗？

sentences.en: I mean, maybe I was super productive because I was off thinking really hard and I wasn't touching my computer much that day, but how can you tell?
sentences.zh: 我是说，也许我当时在苦思冥想，所以效率极高，那天碰电脑不多，但你怎么能看得出来呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that is a question of whether or not what is being monitored actually means anything.
sentences.zh: 所以这就带来了一个问题：被监控的内容究竟有没有实际意义。

sentences.en: Uh, I think this is the big problem right now is that because we have access to the data, we must try to find some sort of meaning from it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为目前最大的问题在于，既然我们能够获取数据，就必须试着从中解读出某种意义。

sentences.en: But like you just illustrated, uh, performance or, uh, how people go about their job related behaviors is a very complex thing.
sentences.zh: 但就像你刚才举例的那样，绩效或者人们如何表现出与工作相关的行为，是一件非常复杂的事情。

sentences.en: Uh, just because I can see that you're free doesn't mean that you're not doing anything.
sentences.zh: 嗯，仅仅因为我看到你有空，并不代表你什么都没做。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that you might be less stressed.
sentences.zh: 这也不代表你的压力可能就更小。

sentences.en: You could have, uh, personal aspects of work that are coming into play as well.
sentences.zh: 工作中可能还有一些个人层面的因素在起作用。

sentences.en: And so I think, uh, organizations are getting closer to monitoring the right things for the right reasons, as long as it's job related and it's not, you know, looking at your
sentences.zh: 因此我认为，只要与工作相关，而不是去窥探你在

sentences.en: personal activity on your personal smartphone or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 个人智能手机上的个人活动之类的事情，组织正越来越趋向于出于正确的理由监控正确的东西。

sentences.en: I think these can be meaningful sources of data, but we just have to be very careful and very deliberate with how they're used.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些可以成为有意义的数据来源，但我们必须非常谨慎，并且深思熟虑地使用它们。

sentences.en: So are they looking at our smartphones now?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们现在是在监视我们的智能手机吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, my, my boss certainly has my cell phone number.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，我的老板肯定有我的手机号。

sentences.en: I think the whole world has my cell phone number.
sentences.zh: 我觉得全世界都有我的手机号。

sentences.en: So who's, who else is watching me?
sentences.zh: 那还有谁在盯着我呢？

sentences.en: And what are they looking for?
sentences.zh: 他们又在寻找什么？

sentences.en: So, uh, we typically talk about, uh, this in terms of like company issued devices.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们通常在公司发放的设备这个层面上来谈论这个问题。

sentences.en: So, uh, there was a case a couple of years ago where, uh, an employee was required to download an app that would help her with, uh, keeping track of clients.
sentences.zh: 几年前发生过这样一件事：一名员工被要求下载一个应用，用来帮她追踪客户。

sentences.en: Um, but it sort of took location information, uh, at the same time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但它同时也会获取位置信息。

sentences.en: Uh, and what this amounted to is the fact that her employer could see how fast she was driving on the highway at any given point.
sentences.zh: 这就意味着，她的雇主可以随时查看她在高速公路上开得多快。

sentences.en: And so those are the sorts of things where it's, it's unintentional, um, with monitoring,
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是那种在监控中并非出于本意的情况，

sentences.en: but that can leave the employee, uh, feeling extremely violated or invaded of their privacy.
sentences.zh: 但这会让员工感到极度被侵犯或隐私受到侵犯。

sentences.en: Uh, when it's not used for its intention, that's when we find employee, uh, reactions to monitoring to be the most negative.
sentences.zh: 当监控没有用于其原本的意图时，我们就会发现员工对监控的反应最为负面。

sentences.en: So what are the next things that you're looking at?
sentences.zh: 那么你接下来要研究的是什么？

sentences.en: So we want to continue looking at, uh, where expectations of monitoring occur and what are the conditions under which monitoring might be accepted?
sentences.zh: 我们希望继续研究对监控的期望在何处产生，以及在什么条件下监控才能被接受？

sentences.en: So we can think of monitoring somebody's sweat levels or biometric levels as something that's very invasive.
sentences.zh: 我们可以认为监测某人的排汗水平或生物特征水平是一件非常具有侵入性的事。

sentences.en: And I think you'd have very few people who'd be willing to give that information to their employer, but what are the circumstances where that's not the case?
sentences.zh: 我想几乎没有人愿意把这些信息交给雇主，但在什么情况下情况会不同呢？

sentences.en: Uh, if I'm monitoring your sweat levels and able to give you a text, um, at three o'clock saying, uh, you've sweat a ridiculous amount on your
sentences.zh: 如果我监测你的排汗水平，并能在三点钟给你发一条信息，说你

sentences.en: construction job, you need to drink some water before you pass out.
sentences.zh: 在建筑工地上出的汗多得离谱，晕倒前得喝点水。

sentences.en: Now the purpose right there is very job related.
sentences.zh: 那么这个目的就与工作高度相关了。

sentences.en: It's very employee focused, it's safety, it's health.
sentences.zh: 它是以员工为中心的，关乎安全和健康。

sentences.en: And so that might be a condition where something, uh, when we just think of it, uh, it might be invasive, but might be acceptable in one situation versus the, versus the next.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种情况可能意味着，某种我们在单独思考时可能觉得具有侵入性的措施，在某种情境下是可以接受的，而在另一种情境下则不然。

sentences.en: So that's something that we really want to look at.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们非常想要研究的课题。

sentences.en: We've expanded, uh, our checklist of how all the people can be, uh, all the ways that people can be monitored, uh, to incorporate some of these newer things like
sentences.zh: 我们扩大了核对清单，涵盖了所有人可能被监控的所有方式，并纳入了一些较新的手段，比如

sentences.en: biometric or facial recognition and are looking, uh, through qualitative data to understand,
sentences.zh: 生物识别或面部识别，并且正通过定性数据来了解，

sentences.en: you know, if somebody thinks that this is sometimes acceptable, what are those circumstances?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果有人认为这在某些时候是可以接受的，那么具体是什么情况？

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, that's all really interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些真的都非常有趣。

sentences.en: I appreciate your coming here today and talking to us about the research that you're performing and look forward to learning more about, uh, whether
sentences.zh: 我很感谢你今天能来到这里，跟我们谈谈你正在进行的研究所，并期待能进一步了解

sentences.en: my boss is watching me or, or not, but I'm going to certainly be a lot more vigilant.
sentences.zh: 我的老板到底有没有在盯着我，不过我肯定会提高警惕。

sentences.en: Uh, before we go, I just want to give everyone a reminder that we want to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 在离开前，我只想提醒大家，我们很想听到你们的声音。

sentences.en: So email your comments and ideas to speaking of psychology at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 请将您的评论和想法发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@APA.org。

sentences.en: And please consider giving us a rating in iTunes.
sentences.zh: 也请考虑在 iTunes 上给我们打分。

sentences.en: That's really helpful for us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is part of the APA podcast network, which includes other informative podcasts, such as APA journals, dialogue about new psychological research
sentences.zh: 《心理学话语》是 APA 播客网络的一部分，其中还包含其他内容丰富的播客，例如探讨新心理学研究的《APA 期刊：对话》

sentences.en: and progress notes about the practice of psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及关于心理学实践的《诊疗札记》。

sentences.en: You can find all our podcasts on Apple,
sentences.zh: 您可以在 Apple、

sentences.en: Stitcher, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: Stitcher 或任何您收听播客的地方找到我们的所有播客。

sentences.en: You can also go to our website, www.speakingofpsychology.org and listen to more episodes.
sentences.zh: 您也可以访问我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 收听更多单集节目。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills with the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 我是美国心理学协会的金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。
